label: Matt 28:1

label: Matt 28:5

label: Matt 28:6
text: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.

variants.reading: the place where he was lying (ho kyrios, 'the Lord', omitted)
variants.note: Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew: ton topon hopou ekeito ('the place where he was positioned') in aleph B Theta 33 892* it(e) syr(s) co, against ton topon hopou ekeito ho kyrios ('the place where the Lord was positioned') in A C D L W Delta 0148 f1 f13 652 Byz.

text: Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”

label: Matt 28:9
text:
As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying,
“Rejoice!”
They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.

label: Matt 28:11
text: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city, and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.

label: Matt 28:13
text: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.

text: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.

label: Matt 28:16
text: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.

text: When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted.

label: Matt 28:19
text:
Go
and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

variants.reading: make disciples of all the nations in my name (en to onomati mou)
variants.note: Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew: Eusebius (Ante-Nicene) cites 'Go make disciples of all the nations in my name', against 'baptizing them into the name of the father and of the son and of the holy spirit' in aleph A B D W f1 f13 Byz; no extant manuscript id for the Eusebius reading is given on the fetched page.

label: Matt 28:20
text: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

label: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to the tomb on the first day of the week
statement: After the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb (28:1).

label: Mary Magdalene came from Magdala
statement: Mary Magdalene ('the Magdalene') is named by her town, Magdala; the attribution rests on the Gospel epithet and later tradition ('It is believed to be the birthplace of Mary Magdalene' per the fetched Magdala article), while excavation confirms the first-century town itself.

label: The week was reckoned from the Sabbath in Judea
statement: In Judea the week ran to the Sabbath, the day of rest; the day after the Sabbath was the first day of the week, and the visit of 28:1 is dated 'after the Sabbath'.

label: An angel of the Lord descended and rolled away the stone
statement: An angel of the Lord descended from the sky, rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it; the guards shook and became like dead men (28:2-4).

label: A great earthquake occurred at the tomb
statement: There was a great earthquake as the angel descended (28:2).

label: The tomb was sealed with a large stone rolled across the entrance
statement: The tomb's entrance was closed by a great stone that was rolled away from the door (28:2). Tension recorded: a documented rolling-stone tomb attests the practice in 1st-century Jerusalem, but the fetched Rock-cut tombs article reports simple tombs closed 'with a rectangular blocking stone or mudbrick', so a round rolling stone is not shown to be the norm; the Kloner rarity survey could not be verified on a fetched page (see notes).

label: Jesus rose from the dead and the tomb was found empty
statement: The angel tells the women, 'He is not here, for he has risen' (28:5-6), and sends them to tell the disciples (28:7).

label: Jesus appeared to the women and to the eleven in Galilee
statement: Jesus met the women as they ran to the disciples (28:9) and the eleven saw him on the Galilean mountain (28:17).

label: The stolen-body report was spread among the Jews
statement: The chief priests had the guards say the disciples stole the body by night while they slept, and 'this saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today' (28:15).

label: The guards reported to the chief priests and were bribed
statement: Some of the guards reported to the chief priests, who gave a large sum of silver and promised to persuade the governor (28:11-14); the story presupposes that a sleeping sentry faced punishment.

label: The eleven went to the mountain in Galilee Jesus appointed
statement: The eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them (28:16); the specific mountain is unidentified (gap).

label: Baptism into the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit
statement: Jesus commissions baptizing 'in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' (28:19); early Christian witnesses know the threefold formula but are reception, never attestation.

label: The movement was commissioned to all the nations and spread beyond Judea
statement: 'Go and make disciples of all nations' (28:19); within a few decades the movement had spread from Judaea to Rome.
